title: Thirty-day flow terms raised nitrate estimation error at two Gulf river outlets in yearly tests for 2000-2025
abstract: We tested whether current flow relative to its preceding 30-day mean improves same-day nitrate plus nitrite estimates at two Gulf river outlets. We used USGS release 3.0 and 767 held-out site-dates in water years 2000-2025. Each fit used the preceding 20 years. Adding two short flow terms raised equal-site mean squared log error by 5.30%. The conditional 95% three-year block interval was an increase of 1.07% to 9.54%. Point error rose at both sites and in all five planned settings. These results give no useful gain for this short flow proxy in the tested estimator. They do not exclude physical hysteresis or gains from other models. Sparse sampling, related river branches, gauge positions, model form, revised data and conditional uncertainty limit inference. The package includes numeric inputs, code, all estimates and resampling draws, an independent numerical audit, provenance and a figure.

display.caption: Annual and equal-site squared log error reductions. Negative values mean higher error. Intervals use common-year blocks and condition on fitted predictions.

citations.reason: Prior year-scale flow-memory test set the short flow question. Same source and overlapping observations; this is not independent confirmation.
